scenes.title: Cold open
narration: The Rhythm of the Sword
This is Dandiya Raas. Historical to modern.
on_screen: Title card: Dandiya Raas · India · Historical to modern

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance originated in Gujarat and Rajasthan during the Gurjara empire.
It is a socio-religious form that has transitioned from a communal, ritualistic practice to a highly structured competitive sport in the collegiate circuit.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The dance is performed during Sharad Navratri, Janmashtami fairs, and weddings.
It represents the battle between the goddess Durga and the demon Mahishasura.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage: Dandiya Raas: A Folk dance form of Gujarat (https://archive.org/details/dni.ncaa.CCRT-156-UMHB)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Dancers operate in pairs, forming two lines that move clockwise.
The basic movement involves an eight-beat cycle where dancers hit their own sticks, then their partner's right and left sticks, before moving on to the next partner in the line.
Watch for stick-clashing.
on_screen: Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: two lines, partners facing each other, moving clockwise
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music follows an eight-beat time cycle called Kaherva.
The primary 'instrument' is the pair of wooden sticks used to mark time and create the percussive sound of the dance.
Listen for the dandiya sticks.
The pulse is 8-beat.
The music is characterized by a rhythmic clattering of sticks marking time, starting slowly and building in intensity.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Kapila Vatsyayan is noted for her work on the aesthetic theory of Rasa, which provides the underlying unity to Indian arts.
Popular forms include Dandiya Raas, Gopgunthan Solanga Raas, and Mer Dandiya Raas.
The dance is a branch of the broader Indian folk dance tradition, with modern competitive Garba-Raas emerging as a distinct style influenced by traditional Dandiya and Garba.
